messages:
Sam R: Quick travel question for the SF offsite: long layover in SFO — anyone prefer a cheap nearby hotel vs. the lounge pass? I can do either but want tips.
Jules T: If it's overnight, hotel beats lounge imo. you actually sleep. I use hotel shuttle + keep a daypack.
Aria V: Agree. Pro tip: book a hotel with 24hr desk and request a late check-in code. cheaper than full night if just sleeping.
Marco P: For short naps the Centurion/priority lounges are great but can be crowded. Also check if your card gives a free lounge pass.
Sam R: Thanks. Any hotel recs within 10-15 min? Trying to avoid long baggage back-and-forth.
Jules T: Holiday Inn Express by the airport is reliable and has shuttle. used it last offsite.
Aria V: There's also the MicroStay option at the SFO airport hotels for 4-6 hour blocks if you only need a nap. search "microstay SFO" before booking.
people-ops-bot: FYI: Reminder: Company reimbursements for overnight layover hotels require manager pre-approval if >1 night. See travel policy: https://intranet/travel-policy
Sam R: Nice, hadn't heard of MicroStay. Also curious: any luggage-storage ideas if I don't want to check in early?
Jules T: Hotel concierge will usually hold a bag for a few hours. or use an app like Bounce to book local storage (cheaper than checking).
Aria V: If you fly in same day as the offsite start, drop luggage at the venue coat check — Ops usually okays it. I'll DM @people-ops with numbers to reserve a small shelf.
Marco P: Poll: react with \ud83d\udea8 = Hotel (overnight), \ud83d\udcab = Lounge, \ud83d\udce6 = Short-term storage or microstay.
Sam R: \ud83d\udea8
Jules T: \ud83d\udea8
Aria V: \ud83d\udcab
